newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Miners strike for the day in Russian Arctic.
newsitem.headline: Miners strike for the day in Russian Arctic.

text.p: Miners in Russia's Arctic Vorkuta region went on a one day-strike on Tuesday over unpaid wages and will decide later in the day whether to make the protest open-ended, their representative said.
Yuri Skrynnikov, an official with the Vorkuta branch of the Independent Union of Miners, said miners had gathered in a central square to decide what to do.
Itar-Tass news agency said employees from other industries in the region, some of them unpaid since February, may join the action, the latest in a series of protests across Russia.
The 11-mine Vorkuta basin, developed by labour camp inmates under Soviet dictator Josef Stalin, is less important than the Kuzbass region in Siberia.
A non-payment crisis of overdue salaries, high inter-enterprise debt and low budget revenues is one of the biggest woes facing the Russian economy, which is otherwise showing some signs of recovery.
In the far eastern region of Primorye, officials were preparing to cut energy supplies to apartment buildings due to fuel shortages at power stations, Interfax news agency said.
Miners and power workers there have struck repeatedly over overdue salaries.
